### How it works

If a string consists of repeated copies of a shorter block, rotating it by one block produces the same string. Doubling the string contains all such rotations. Removing the first and last positions excludes the two trivial matches, leaving a match exactly when a proper repeat exists.

### Steps

1. Build s + s.
2. Remove its first and last characters.
3. Check whether s occurs in the remaining string.

### Complexity

- Time: Conservative O(n²) worst-case substring search; library implementations may be faster.
- Space: O(n) for the doubled string and substring.

### Things to watch for

- Exclude both trivial boundary matches.
- A one-character string cannot repeat a shorter nonempty block.
- The returned answer is a boolean, not the repeated block.
